The '''revenant dragon''' is the spirit of a [[Dragon (race)|dragon]] that inhabits the [[Forinthry Dungeon]], along with all other [[revenants]]. They are the strongest revenants, and only appear in members' worlds.
The Forinthry Dungeon is a part of the [[Wilderness]] so it is possible to be attacked by other players here if opted into [[PvP]].

Like all revenants, they can restore lifepoints quickly, can cure themselves of poison and react quickly to a player's protection prayers. When below 50% health, revenant dragons will "eat" to heal 1275 lifepoints from their limited supply of food. For a full description of the healing mechanic see the [[Revenants#Overview|revenants]] page.

Revenant dragons are the only revenants capable of inflicting [[poison]], doing so via their ranged attacks, dealing around 400-800 each time a poison hit is inflicted. They also possess unusually high defensive stats for their level, comparable to that of high-level bosses (their affinities and Defence level are the same as [[Vorago]]'s, but their armour is even higher).

Despite being former dragons, [[dragon slayer (effect)|dragon slayer effects]] do not work on them; instead, [[undead slayer (effect)|undead slayer effects]] do. They do not use dragonfire either.

==Drops==
{{DropLogProject|jagex=yes}}

Revenant drops are not affected by [[luck]]. There are only two ways to increase the drop rate of revenant items: completion of the [[elite Wilderness achievements]] which gives a 5% increased chance for revenant drops, and [[revenant drop enhancer]]s, which give a 10% increased chance. Both boosts can be in effect at the same time.

==Trivia==
* Revenant dragons had two heads before the dragon graphical update on [[5 July]] [[2010]].
* Prior to the Evolution of Combat, revenant dragons were the strongest revenants. After the update, their combat level was lowered for unknown reasons; however, a subsequent update returned them back to their original position.
* Despite possessing the appearances of an adult dragon, revenant dragons are unusually smaller compared to their living counterparts; all other revenants occupy the same amount of tiles as with their living counterparts. An adult dragon covers a 5 × 5 area, while a revenant dragon only covers a 2 × 2 area.
